title: &&, || and !
summary: Combining true/false values, and the ternary shortcut.

say.never: You can combine true/false questions. `&&` means **and** (both must be true). `||` means **or** (at least one is true). `!` means **not** and flips true to false. For example `has_comms && !e_stopped` reads: "we have comms AND we're not e-stopped".
say.bit: `&&` is **and** (both true), `||` is **or** (at least one), `!` is **not** (flip it).

board.code:
has_comms && !e_stopped    // comms AND not e-stopped
day.equals("Saturday") || day.equals("Sunday")

say.never: To check if two pieces of text match, use `.equals(...)`. The `==` sign doesn't compare the letters. It asks "are these the very same object?", which usually gives the wrong answer for text. So always write `day.equals("Sunday")`.
say.bit: Use `.equals(...)` for Strings, not `==`. `==` asks "same object?", which is usually not what you mean.

board.code:
day.equals("Sunday")   // compares the text
day == "Sunday"        // compares objects: unreliable

say.never: The **ternary** is a one-line shortcut for if/else that hands back a value. Read `is_reversed ? "REVERSED" : "FORWARD"` as: "if is_reversed is true, give me REVERSED, otherwise give me FORWARD".
say.bit: `condition ? a : b` is a one-line if/else that **gives back a value**.
